newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais urged to seek psychiatric help for woes.
newsitem.headline: Thais urged to seek psychiatric help for woes.

text.p: Thais are being urged to let out their economic frustrations on psychiatrist's couches instead of on the street.
Deputy Public Health Minister Sorahart Klinprathum said on Thursday that Thais should relieve stress from economic pains by consulting psychiatrists rather than staging street protests.

"People who feel the stress from the IMF (International Monetary Fund)-advised suspension of finance firms should visit psychiatrists. They should relax with psychiatrists rather than taking to the streets. Don't fear you would be seen as insane," he said.

A decision by the Bank of Thailand on Tuesday to suspend 42 cash-strapped finance companies has sent shockwaves through the Thai financial sector, triggering public runs on deposits at other sound financial institutions.
Thailand's growing economic problems have spawned rumours of a possible coup by the armed forces against Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and talk of street protests in the capital.

"I deposited more than one million baht in a suspended finance firm. I don't know when I can get my money back," one woman told Reuters. "I've heard that hundreds of disgruntled depositors plan to stage a street protest."
Sorahart last week called on fortune tellers to help cheer up depressed Thais, who normally seek their advice during important occasions of their lives.
